ports.intent: Retain content-only automation, explicit test-build privileges, virtual-authenticator routing and correct navigation realm lifetime.
invariants: WebDriver remains dormant unless an explicit automation flag is supplied and its Gecko listeners stay loopback-only.
Desktop Embedder cannot enable parent-process system access through either the command line or environment.
Marionette exposes no Addon:Install, Addon:Uninstall or chrome-context switch command in a Desktop Embedder package.
WebDriver BiDi exposes no webExtension module and packages neither its extension mutation module nor the shared Addon helper.
Desktop Embedder sessions are projected through the reusable tab registry so WebDriver discovers, creates, activates and closes content contexts without reaching into product UI code.
The Desktop Embedder tab adapter forwards frame-loader event observation to its owning chrome window so Marionette can track process switches without Firefox gBrowser.
Desktop Embedder automation exposes only the product's default user context and does not restore the excluded container-identity service.
The minimal devtools/platform SpiderMonkey Debugger bridge required by WebDriver script realms is retained without the DevTools client, server, shared framework or startup integration.
Navigation, content DOM/JavaScript, input, network observation, screenshots and lifecycle commands remain available.
Firefox and other non-Desktop-Embedder products retain their upstream WebDriver extension and privileged-debug behavior.
Desktop Embedder production builds continue to reject parent-process system access even when the command-line flag or environment variable is supplied.
Only an ENABLE_TESTS build with the explicit upstream system-access opt-in can enter chrome context for Gecko-owned harness setup.
Marionette retains SetContext so content-only automation works; requesting chrome context still requires system access.
The WPT mach command recognizes a generic Desktop Embedder build without making the product pretend to be Firefox.
Test-only managed extension storage is ignored in every production build and may only provide deterministic policy to reviewed application built-ins in an ENABLE_TESTS build.
Only the existing privileged WebDriver/XPCOM virtual-authenticator commands can create the routing condition; Web content cannot register or discover a test token.

While at least one virtual authenticator exists, registration, assertion, UVPAA and conditional-autofill discovery use the virtual-token manager; removing the last authenticator immediately restores the configured production route.
Production soft-token and USB-token preferences remain unchanged and may stay locked; a normal browser session continues to use native authenticators only.
Virtual authenticator consent is governed by the WebDriver isUserConsenting and isUserVerified state, while real USB operations retain the native presence prompt and all existing PIN/device flows.
The port changes no WebAuthn DOM API, credential serialization, relying-party validation or non-desktop platform service selection.
Only successfully created privileged virtual-authenticator IDs enter the top-level WebAuthn service's active set.
While that set is nonempty, registration, assertion and conditional credential discovery use authenticator-rs on Windows, macOS and other native-provider platforms.
Successful removal deletes the exact ID, and removing the last virtual authenticator restores the native production provider for later ceremonies.
The route does not unlock the software-token preference, expose authenticator IDs to Web content or create a production software fallback.
Each WindowRealm captures the inner-window identity of the global for which its automation features were enabled.
Destroying a realm disables async-stack and unlimited-stack capture only while that same inner window remains the current global.
Tab removal, same-origin navigation and cross-origin navigation cannot make obsolete-realm cleanup touch the replacement global or emit a chrome://remote Realm error.
Normal cleanup of a live current global remains intact, and the production content-only WebDriver boundary does not regain add-on installation or another privileged product surface.

ports.intent: Retain current PermissionsPolicy headers, final-origin container inheritance, object/embed publication and sync-XHR enforcement.
invariants: Content exposes document.permissionsPolicy and iframe.permissionsPolicy but not the obsolete featurePolicy aliases.
The structured Permissions-Policy header accepts self, wildcard, scheme, host and port source expressions and ignores the obsolete Feature-Policy response header.
Header policy, iframe allow policy, nested inheritance, sandboxed opaque origins and cross-process container policy compose without granting a feature denied by an ancestor.
Synchronous XHR is advertised with a default-all allowlist and throws NetworkError from send() when policy disables it.
The selected WPT metadata records no expected failures for behavior covered by this port.

Serialized container policy keeps the embedding document origin, inherited denials and modern HTTP declaration separately from iframe declarations and the original src. The final loaded principal determines inherited access; src retains its original meaning.

Reconstruct the embedding document with the Permissions-Policy header parser and the container with the iframe parser. Recompute both restrictions for the final origin; a prospective-src allow or denial cannot authorize or reject a different final origin by itself.

A loaded document copies the evaluated container decision once and retains its own response policy. Same-process, remote, iframe, object and embed paths share that rule; missing or inconsistent parent identity fails closed.
LoadObject refreshes and publishes container policy after successful docshell creation and before handing the channel to the document loader. UpgradeLoadToDocument uses that shared path.
The snapshot retains exact embedding document and browsing context ownership, origin and inherited policy. Missing or inactive frame state cannot publish authority.
Parent authorization still rejects absent or stale canonical container metadata. This change does not relax response policy, origin delegation or product API exposure locks.
ports.port_review: Exercise extracted production inheritance, serialization inputs and final-origin decisions with recorded parser/principal peers, plus existing parent-policy and revocation regression checks. Compile the actual FeaturePolicy, document, container and IPC consumers with configured target headers. Replay same-origin/cross-origin redirects, explicit and default delegation, parent and child header restrictions, live policy loss and malformed/stale ownership in current packaged browsers; extracted tests do not establish actual parsing, IPC or native browser behavior. Reproduce missing publication with the original document-load arm, then exercise corrected load ordering, local/remote frame state, failures and refreshed owner/origin under sanitizers. Compile the full changed translation unit against configured target headers. Replay object/embed direct and redirected loads in current packaged browsers together with iframe delegation and live policy revocation. Recorded loader, policy and IPC peers are not native browser evidence.

A disallowed client returns no records even when an old profile database exists. Production allowed clients read immutable packaged records and timestamps; mutable profile data, signature URLs and forced-sync preferences cannot supersede the package.

The Navis Gradle settings branch includes only annotations, navis-runtime-android and navis product projects; GeckoView, Android Components and example projects remain isolated to upstream product branches.

The Navis application has one engine dependency on its private navis-runtime-android module mounted from the canonical runtime/android source root, and no GeckoView project, published AAR or broad GeckoView source dependency.

The private runtime compiles a reviewed Java primitive allowlist; product sources and the packaged DEX contain no GeckoRuntime, GeckoSession, GeckoView, GeckoDisplay or other excluded lifecycle-owner definition or type reference.
Navis SDK bindings and generated JNI wrappers are produced by navis-runtime-android rather than requiring the GeckoView Gradle project.
Generated manifest, child-process, XPCOM error and crash-report sources are projected into the selected runtime module's object directory.
Navis native libraries and assets stage under dist/navis-android, and candidate packaging verifies that owned stage rather than accepting dist/geckoview.
The non-Navis branch retains the selected ESR's GeckoView project, generated-source tasks and dist/geckoview staging behavior.
Only the Navis Android runtime adds the library notice; desktop packaging does not claim the Android UI dependency.
The packaged modules/navis-licenses path matches the fixed resource URI in the shared offline credits reader.
The application-owned notice preserves the unmodified pinned upstream Apache 2.0 license and attribution.
This resource declaration does not change native code, JNI, extension policy or the Kotlin/Compose toolchain.
Each profile selects a distinct child-service class namespace before Gecko parent startup.
Socket, GPU, RDD, utility and content service ownership cannot cross profile parents.
Notification and Runtime registration use the same final profile namespace contract.
The Navis Gradle variant follows developer_options: Debug for development and Release for --enable-release; generated JNI wrappers and APK assembly use that same variant.
Named event-dispatcher cleanup is safe before native attachment, after native window detachment and on repeated close; an old owner cannot remove its replacement.
ports.port_review: Review the Android lifecycle, JNI/native and Gradle graphs, staged module/resource inventory and profile-selected child-service namespaces together against the selected Gecko pin. Preserve upstream GeckoView consumers and the stated Core, security and ownership boundaries; validate the complete ordered series and native Android startup, process isolation, crash and relaunch paths.

ports.intent: Expose the final Android extension host, cold-start readiness, real product tabs/windows/profile APIs and local developer policy without a remote debugger listener.
invariants: One process-wide host exposes real Navis tabs, windows, profile data and extension inventory only after product and startup Session readiness.
Built-ins, signed profile packages and explicitly enabled temporary development retain distinct admission and permission policies; no online store or filesystem bypass is introduced.
Developer mode uses the product preference and temporary-extension policy; in-app DevTools never enables a remote debugger listener.
Optional/private permissions are transactional and checked against the current extension, tab, window and document; unsupported API operations fail closed.
Bookmarks, topSites, history, closed sessions and window actions consume actual product stores and commit events, not simulated parallel state.
Shared command/API registration includes the separately implemented downloads, context actions, popup and search capabilities; ordinary upstream GeckoView behavior remains separate.

Android startup packages CertificateSecurity and CertificateSecurityData and initializes the same bundled certificate-security consumer as desktop; the shared settings adapter owns immutable local data and transport denial.

invariants: Existing editable Binder methods remain the transport; no Console-specific character filtering or duplicate suppression is used.

ports.intent: Bind login selection/save authorization to the originating document and acknowledge only committed Keystore/SQLite writes.
invariants: Engine-private candidates retain credential secrets; Platform prompt DTOs contain metadata and an opaque selection index only.
Actual Session privacy, request identity and callback ownership are checked before persistence; duplicate submissions and late results cannot resolve replacement prompts.
Storage exceptions, failed inserts and transaction commit failures propagate through the Java/Kotlin bridge; enqueue alone never reports success.
Gecko observers and native prompt completion follow commit, without issuing a duplicate storage write.
Closing a prompt withdraws presentation ownership, not a promise to undo an already accepted storage transaction. Document/POST association remains a separate required audit.
Save tokens are parent-owned and browser-scoped; Java checks their authority before entering the retained commit transaction, never after writing credentials.
A normal form submission may survive its HTTP redirect using the replacement document channel's triggeringWindowId and isFormSubmission; URL similarity cannot grant that authority.
Same-document successful fetch/removal remains valid; unrelated navigation, native presentation, private saves, superseded prompts and foreign tokens are rejected.
Selections fill only through the captured WindowGlobal actor; old actor destruction or pagehide cannot cancel another document's new prompt.
HTTP authentication tokens originate only from the real AuthPrompter, not an arbitrary httpRealm value; existing challenge behaviour is retained without claiming new per-channel challenge validation.
Shared code enters the new host path only for Navis Android; desktop does not require a native source token or gain an Android lifecycle owner.

Android settings cache Core projections and never write a parallel search configuration.
Private Sessions never issue remote suggestions; opt-in, query classification, cancellation and stale-document guards stay inside Core.
Local bookmark/history/tab candidates remain bounded Profile values; private history and foreign-mode tabs are excluded.
Live extension catalogue and named/default submissions use Gecko without new extension permissions.
Only product:initialize accepts a 512KiB legacy payload; ordinary operations retain 64KiB bounds.

ports.intent: Use complete reviewed upstream certificate data and enforce an immutable offline OneCRL baseline before the first TLS verification.
invariants: Every Navis TLS trust decision checks the complete packaged OneCRL issuer/serial and subject/SPKI-hash baseline before mutable certificate storage. Existing profiles, offline startup and async import cannot weaken it.

Trust data is the complete official NSS root-list snapshot with its matching library version header. Every upstream addition, removal and trust change is retained; NSS implementation follows the selected Gecko baseline and user-root CT boundaries remain intact.
Navis explicitly enforces CT mode 2 on all targets including Android and persisted old-profile values. The upstream metadata expiry safeguard remains unchanged.
The applicable upstream OneCRL startup import fix initializes the normal cert_storage consumer; it is additional to the immutable native baseline.

ports.intent: Retain page hover for the entire chrome-owned context-menu lifetime, including pointer movement outside the popup, then restore normal pointer hit testing on closure.
invariants: Only Desktop Embedder builds suppress content mouse move/enter/exit, and only while a context menu remains open in the same chrome document. Parent remote-target bookkeeping can still leave the actor, preserving other-window input.

Deferred exits and the last real pointer event retain parent coordinates and follow the existing BrowserParent IPC path. Closure releases exits before restoring only the latest real target, including precise Fission targets, then requests native pointer hit testing. No CSS locks, content script suppression, new public capability or remote service is introduced.
Actual menu closure releases every affected Fission frame. Submenu closure does not clear page hover while the parent context menu is still open, and another window is unaffected.
Saved addresses and originating documents remain private to Runtime. Hidden or removed address targets remain usable only for the current offered, enabled, single-use menu request.
